key: Your very question shows that you knew I knew.
s: On the Hao bridge, Hui Tzŭ denies anyone but a fish can know its pleasure; Guo Xiang, on 17.149, reads it as saying no one need be a fish to know fishes, since Hui Tzŭ knew Chuang Tzŭ was no fish without being him.
src: Guo Xiang, Zhuangzi zhu, chapter 17, on 17.149, zh.wikisource (Nanhua zhenjing zhushu, juan 19, Zhengtong Daozang), revision 7907030 (2026)

opened.edition: zh.wikisource 南華真經註疏 卷十九 (Zhengtong Daozang, DZ0745), revision 7907030, Cheng Xuanying's shu left out
opened.locator: chapter 17, Guo Xiang's note on 莊子曰：請循其本。子曰汝安知魚樂云者……我知之濠上也 (Giles 17.149 to 17.151)

evidence.words: 今子非我也，而云汝安知魚樂者，是知我之非魚也。苟知我之非魚，則凡相知者，果可以此知彼，不待是魚然後知魚也。
evidence.gloss: Now you are not I, yet in saying 'how do you know the pleasure of fish' you know that I am not a fish. If you know I am not a fish, then all who know one another can indeed know that one from this one, and need not be a fish before knowing fish.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref Zhuangzi 17.149, at 1605). The packet aligns Guo Xiang's note to the Chinese 請循其本 ... 我知之濠上也, which opens at Giles 17.149 and corresponds to the key verse; opening words confirmed. Guo Xiang's own words say Hui Tzu, not being Zhuangzi, still knew he was no fish, so knowing need not wait on being a fish: exactly the reading given, no drift. His neighbouring note on 17.147 makes the same point. Plain sense matches 17.146 to 17.148 of day.js. entry-check ok with no errors or warnings.
